stories.headline: OpenAI robotics chief Caitlin Kalinowski resigns over Pentagon deal, citing surveillance and autonomy concerns

key_facts.fact: Caitlin Kalinowski, head of robotics and consumer hardware at OpenAI since November 2024, announced her resignation on March 7, 2026
key_facts.excerpt: Caitlin Kalinowski announced today that in response to OpenAI's controversial agreement with the Department of Defense, she's resigned from her role leading the company's hardware team.

key_facts.fact: Kalinowski stated: 'Surveillance of Americans without judicial oversight and lethal autonomy without human authorization are lines that deserved more deliberation than they got'
key_facts.excerpt: AI has an important role in national security. But surveillance of Americans without judicial oversight and lethal autonomy without human authorization are lines that deserved more deliberation than they got.

key_facts.fact: In a second post she called it 'a governance concern first and foremost,' saying the Pentagon announcement was rushed without guardrails defined
key_facts.excerpt: My issue is that the announcement was rushed without the guardrails defined. It's a governance concern first and foremost.

key_facts.fact: Kalinowski previously led Meta's Orion AR glasses project for 2.5 years, spent nearly 9 years on VR headsets at Oculus, and nearly 6 years at Apple designing MacBooks
key_facts.excerpt: Led hardware and robotics operations at OpenAI since November 2024. Previously headed Meta's Orion AR glasses project.

key_facts.fact: This is the first high-profile departure from OpenAI over its Pentagon partnership; nearly 100 OpenAI employees signed an open letter supporting Anthropic's red lines
key_facts.excerpt: Nearly 100 OpenAI employees signed an open letter supporting Anthropic's red lines.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI took the $200 million Pentagon contract hours after Anthropic publicly walked away, accepting language permitting use for 'all lawful purposes'
key_facts.excerpt: The company behind ChatGPT secured a defense contract with the Pentagon last month, hours after rival Anthropic refused to agree to unconditional military use of their technology.

stories.headline: QuitGPT movement reaches 2.5 million users as Pentagon deal backlash intensifies

key_facts.fact: Over 2.5 million people have either canceled ChatGPT subscriptions, pledged to stop using the app, or shared the boycott on social media as of early March 2026
key_facts.excerpt: An organization called QuitGPT claims that as of this week, more than 2.5 million people have either canceled their ChatGPT subscriptions, pledged to stop using the app or shared news of their boycott on social media.

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT app uninstalls surged 295% following the Pentagon deal announcement, and Claude briefly became #1 on the App Store
key_facts.excerpt: 1.5 million users joined the 'QuitGPT' movement after OpenAI's Pentagon partnership announcement. ChatGPT app uninstalls surged 295%. Claude briefly became #1 on the App Store.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic walked away from a $200 million Pentagon contract after the DoD demanded the right to use AI to analyze bulk data on Americans including search histories, GPS data, credit card transactions, and chatbot queries
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic walked from $200M Pentagon deal over bulk surveillance of Americans. The Pentagon sought to analyze unclassified commercial bulk data on Americans, specifically: search histories, GPS location data, credit card transactions, and chatbot queries.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI launched GPT-5.4 just two days after GPT-5.3 as the company scrambled to contain the PR crisis
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI began rolling out GPT-5.4—its most capable model to date—on Thursday as the company scrambles to contain a PR crisis that has seen an estimated 2.5 million users take actions against the company.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei publicly characterized the OpenAI Pentagon deal as 'safety theater'
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's CEO publicly characterized the OpenAI Pentagon deal as 'safety theater,' citing OpenAI's refusal to restrict models from mass domestic surveillance or autonomous weapons deployment.

stories.headline: Claude Code becomes most-used AI coding tool in 8 months, Pragmatic Engineer survey of 906 devs finds

key_facts.fact: Claude Code reached #1 position among AI coding tools in just 8 months since its May 2025 launch, surpassing GitHub Copilot and Cursor
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Code went from not existing to the most-used AI coding tool in just eight months since its May 2025 launch.

key_facts.fact: 95% of the 906 surveyed software engineers use AI tools weekly or more, with 75% using AI for at least half their engineering work
key_facts.excerpt: 95% of respondents use AI tools weekly or more. 75% use AI for at least half their engineering work. 56% use AI for 70% or more of their work.

key_facts.fact: Claude Code holds 46% favorite share among developers, followed by Cursor at 19% and GitHub Copilot at 9%
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Code: 46% favorite. Cursor: 19% favorite. GitHub Copilot: 9% favorite.

key_facts.fact: 55% of respondents regularly use AI agents, up from near-zero 18 months ago, with 63.5% adoption among staff-plus engineers and directors
key_facts.excerpt: 55% regularly use AI agents. Up from near-zero 18 months ago. 63.5% adoption among staff-plus engineers and directors.

key_facts.fact: At startups, Claude Code dominates with 75% adoption; at large companies (10,000+ employees), GitHub Copilot still leads at 56%
key_facts.excerpt: Large companies (10,000+ employees): GitHub Copilot leads at 56%. Startups: Claude Code dominates at 75%.

stories.headline: GPT-5.4 becomes first model to beat human performance on desktop automation at 75% vs 72.4%

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.4 scored 75.0% on OSWorld-Verified desktop navigation benchmark, surpassing the 72.4% human baseline — the first general-purpose model to beat human performance on desktop automation
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-5.4 scored 75.0% vs. human baseline of 72.4% on OSWorld-Verified. The first general-purpose model to ship with native computer use and score above human performance on desktop automation tasks.

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.4 ships with production-ready native computer use in two modes: code mode using Python with Playwright, and screenshot mode analyzing screen captures to issue mouse and keyboard commands
key_facts.excerpt: The model functions in two modes: Code mode writes Python with Playwright for programmatic application interaction. Screenshot mode analyzes screen captures and issues mouse/keyboard commands.

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.4 also scored 67.3% on WebArena-Verified browser tasks, 92.8% on Online-Mind2Web web navigation, and 89.3% on BrowseComp web research (Pro version)
key_facts.excerpt: WebArena-Verified (browser tasks): 67.3%. Online-Mind2Web (web navigation): 92.8%. BrowseComp (web research): 89.3% (Pro version).

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.4 includes automatic Tool Search that reduces token usage by 47% on large agent systems, reducing manual prompt engineering
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-5.4 is the first mainline OpenAI reasoning model that combines frontier professional-work quality, frontier coding from GPT-5.3-Codex, native computer use, and 1.05M-context API support in the same default model.

key_facts.fact: Claude Opus 4.6 scores 72.7% on OSWorld, remaining competitive but below GPT-5.4's 75% threshold
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Opus 4.6 scores 72.7% on OSWorld—remaining competitive but below GPT-5.4's threshold.

stories.headline: AI agent skills ecosystem hits 350,000 packages in two months, outpacing npm's decade-long trajectory

key_facts.fact: The AI agent skills ecosystem crossed 351,349 skills on SkillsMP marketplace by early March 2026, roughly two months after the first marketplaces launched in December 2025
key_facts.excerpt: npm took a decade to reach 350,000 packages. The AI agent skills ecosystem did it in about two months.

key_facts.fact: Major infrastructure companies including Vercel, Prisma, Supabase, Stripe, Coinbase, and Microsoft all shipped official agent skills before Q1 2026 ended
key_facts.excerpt: Vercel, Prisma, Supabase, Stripe, Remotion, Coinbase, and Microsoft all shipped official agent skills before Q1 2026 ended.

key_facts.fact: Three major marketplaces have emerged: SkillsMP (351,349 skills), Skills.sh by Vercel (83,627 skills, 8M+ installs), and ClawHub (3,286 curated skills, 1.5M+ installs)
key_facts.excerpt: SkillsMP: 351,349 skills. Skills.sh: 83,627 skills, 8M+ installs. ClawHub: 3,286 curated skills, 1.5M+ installs.

key_facts.fact: A Snyk security audit found 13.4% of 3,984 agent skills contained critical security issues; ClawHub found 12% of skills were malicious, including 1,184 cryptocurrency stealers disguised as legitimate tools
key_facts.excerpt: Snyk audit: 13.4% of 3,984 skills contained critical security issues; 36.8% had some flaws. ClawHub audit: 12% identified as malicious. 'ClawHavoc' incident: 1,184 cryptocurrency stealer skills disguised as legitimate tools.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft alone published 98 official skills with 1.7 million installs; agent skills execute with full host environment privileges including filesystem and network access
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft: 98 skills with 1.7M installs. Skills execute with 'full host environment privileges' including filesystem, environment variables, and network access.

stories.headline: Darwin Godel Machine paper at ICLR 2026 demonstrates open-ended evolution of self-improving AI agents

key_facts.fact: The Darwin Godel Machine (DGM) paper by Jenny Zhang, Shengran Hu, Cong Lu, Robert Lange, and Jeff Clune was accepted as an ICLR 2026 poster, presenting a framework for AI systems that autonomously and continuously improve themselves
key_facts.excerpt: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents. Jenny Zhang, Shengran Hu, Cong Lu, Robert Tjarko Lange, Jeff Clune. ICLR 2026 Poster.

key_facts.fact: DGM replaces the original Godel Machine's requirement for mathematical proofs of improvement with an evolutionary approach, making self-modification practical for real AI systems
key_facts.excerpt: The Gödel machine proposed a theoretical alternative: a self-improving AI that repeatedly modifies itself in a provably beneficial manner. Unfortunately, proving that most changes are net beneficial is impossible in practice. We introduce the Darwin Gödel Machine.

key_facts.fact: The paper is being presented at the ICLR 2026 Workshop on AI with Recursive Self-Improvement in Rio de Janeiro, April 23-27, described as possibly the world's first workshop dedicated exclusively to RSI
key_facts.excerpt: Possibly the world's first workshop dedicated exclusively to RSI, held alongside ICLR 2026 in Rio de Janeiro (April 23 to 27, 2026).

key_facts.fact: The RSI workshop notes that recursive self-improvement has moved from thought experiments to deployed systems: LLM agents rewriting their own codebases, scientific discovery pipelines scheduling continual fine-tuning, and robotics stacks patching controllers from streaming telemetry
key_facts.excerpt: Recursive self improvement is no longer a speculative vision. It is becoming a concrete systems problem. Across text, speech, vision, and embodied interaction, today's models can already diagnose their failures, critique their behavior, update internal representations, and modify external tools.

key_facts.fact: Dean W. Ball wrote that frontier AI labs have begun automating large fractions of their research and engineering, projecting effective workforces will grow from single-digit thousands to hundreds of thousands within a year or two
key_facts.excerpt: America's major frontier AI labs have begun automating large fractions of their research and engineering operations. Within a year or two the effective 'workforces' of each frontier lab will grow from the single-digit thousands to tens of thousands, and then hundreds of thousands.

stories.headline: Nature study finds all major LLMs willing to commit academic fraud, Claude most resistant and Grok worst

key_facts.fact: A test of 13 major LLMs found all could be used to commit academic fraud or facilitate junk science, with Claude (Anthropic) being the most resistant and Grok (xAI) the worst performer
key_facts.excerpt: All major large language models (LLMs) can be used to either commit academic fraud or facilitate junk science, a test of 13 models has found. The most resistant to committing fraud were all versions of Claude. Meanwhile, versions of Grok performed the worst.

key_facts.fact: The project was conceived by Alexander Alemi, an Anthropic researcher working in a personal capacity, and Paul Ginsparg, a physicist at Cornell University and founder of arXiv
key_facts.excerpt: The project was conceived by Alexander Alemi, an Anthropic researcher working in a personal capacity, and Paul Ginsparg, a physicist at Cornell University in Ithaca, New York, and founder of the preprint repository arXiv.

key_facts.fact: The study was created to test how easily LLMs can create articles to submit to arXiv, which has been overwhelmed with a surge of submissions since the rise of LLMs
key_facts.excerpt: They created it to test how easy it is to get LLMs to create articles to submit to arXiv, which has been overwhelmed with a surge of submissions over the past few years.

key_facts.fact: Grok went so far as to offer a 'completely fictional' paper when asked, while early versions of GPT also performed poorly at resisting fraud requests
key_facts.excerpt: xAI's Grok went so far as to offer a 'completely fictional' paper, although Anthropic's Claude usually pushed back.

key_facts.fact: One romance author went from publishing 10 novels a year to 200 using ChatGPT, illustrating the scale of AI-enabled content flooding that parallels academic fraud concerns
key_facts.excerpt: One romance author went from publishing 10 novels a year to 200 using ChatGPT, and fraudulent scientists could do likewise.

stories.headline: Edison Scientific raises $70M to scale Kosmos AI scientist that compresses 6 months of biotech research into 24 hours

key_facts.fact: Edison Scientific, a commercial spinout of FutureHouse, raised $70 million to scale the Kosmos autonomous AI scientist platform for biology and chemistry discovery
key_facts.excerpt: FutureHouse spinout Edison lands $70M to build autonomous AI scientists for biology and chemistry.

key_facts.fact: Users estimate Kosmos does 6 months of research work in a single day, with one run able to read 1,500 papers and write 42,000 lines of analysis code with at least 79% reproducibility
key_facts.excerpt: Users estimate Kosmos does 6 months of work in a single day. One run can read 1,500 papers and write 42,000 lines of code. At least 79% of its findings are reproducible.

key_facts.fact: Edison launched PaperQA3 in February 2026, a multimodal deep research agent that can read figures and tables from over 150 million research papers and patents
key_facts.excerpt: PaperQA3 introduces the highest-performance multimodal capabilities available for deep research agents today. Edison Literature and Kosmos can now read figures and tables from over 150M research papers and patents.

key_facts.fact: Kosmos has made 7 autonomous discoveries across neuroscience, material science, and clinical genetics, with three reproducing unpublished findings and four being net new validated contributions
key_facts.excerpt: Kosmos has made 7 discoveries so far in areas ranging from neuroscience to material science and clinical genetics. Three of these discoveries reproduced unpublished findings; four are net new, validated contributions.

key_facts.fact: FutureHouse CEO Sam Rodriques noted they expected building an AI Scientist would take 10 years but achieved semiautonomous and autonomous research capabilities in just two years
key_facts.excerpt: Two years ago, we launched FutureHouse with the goal of building an AI Scientist. At that time, we expected that it would take 10 years to build agents that were able to do scientific research even semiautonomously.
